items.what_in_silico_did: Reproduced the documented I-A(d) register for cOVA323-339 (core VHAAHAEIN, %Rank 0.17), confirming the hybridoma system's restriction element behaves as published.
items.what_it_cannot_do: IL-2 secretion is a cellular functional readout. No sequence model predicts cytokine output. Binding is necessary, not sufficient.

items.verdict: NO for the comparison the step is built around
items.what_in_silico_did: Scored 2 of 6 panel members. The 17-mer uniblock and the 30-mer diblock return the same core at the same %Rank, i.e. appending the assembly block changes nothing a sequence model can see.
items.what_it_cannot_do: 2 peptides sit below the class II API's 11-residue floor and cannot be submitted at all. 2 contain D-amino acids, which no class II predictor represents — a D-substituted peptide is scored as its all-L twin, which is a different molecule. Since Step 1 is an all-L control versus D-substituted test comparison, in-silico cannot perform it.

items.rfp_item: Step 2 · cell-free peptide-MHC binding / stability screen
items.what_in_silico_did: Measured NetMHCpan on these two alleles specifically, against every labelled IEDB record for them: HLA-A*32:01 AUC 0.912; HLA-B*57:01 AUC 0.923. That converts the pre-screen from an opinion into a calibrated rule: HLA-A*32:01 skip at %Rank>=2.0 (NPV 0.97); HLA-B*57:01 skip at %Rank>=20.0 (NPV 0.95).
items.what_it_cannot_do: Predicts binding, not complex stability or off-rate. The RFP asks for stability, which is the property that governs whether a tetramer survives staining, and no sequence model reports a half-life.

items.rfp_item: Step 2 · custom synthesis of 2 alleles + 8 uniblock complexes
items.verdict: DE-RISK — this is where the money is
items.what_in_silico_did: Ranked all 10 possible (peptide, allele) complexes and called 7 worth building. A monomer that does not fold never becomes a tetramer, and that is discovered after the spend.
items.what_it_cannot_do: Cannot confirm refolding, biotinylation or multimerisation yield. A predicted binder can still fail to refold.

items.rfp_item: Step 2 · baseline precursor frequency by FACS after IL-7/IL-15 expansion
items.what_in_silico_did: Nothing. There is no sequence-level surrogate.
items.what_it_cannot_do: Precursor frequency is a property of one donor's T-cell repertoire, set by their thymic selection and exposure history. It is measured, not predicted. This is the single most irreplaceable item in the RFP.
Proliferation and cytokine output are cellular outcomes downstream of processing, presentation, co-stimulation and repertoire. Sequence models see only the first step.

items.rfp_item: Donors · human PBMC carrying the specified HLA antigens
items.verdict: DE-RISK — and it may change the study design
items.what_in_silico_did: Carrier frequency, weighted US/EU: HLA-A*32:01 5.7%, HLA-B*57:01 5.9%, either 11.2%, both 0.35%. To obtain 10 donors: ~89 typed if either allele suffices, ~2882 if each donor must carry both.
items.what_it_cannot_do: Cannot tell you what a commercial HLA-typed bank already holds, and the two-locus combination assumes independence, which linkage disequilibrium violates.

headline: No item in this RFP can be replaced by computation. Three of 7 can be materially de-risked before commissioning: the binding pre-screen, the tetramer build list, and donor feasibility. The wet-lab study should still be run — but it should be a smaller, better-targeted one.
